findings.title: Customers and drivers are quoted materially wrong fares for real routes — the server substitutes straight-line distance and a fixed speed for road routing
findings.observed: Both estimates and bookings use haversine distance × 1.3 and vehicle speed, not road routes.

findings.title: Riders can be assigned an unsuitable vehicle or courier — dispatch matches only vehicle type, not the booked service or vehicle option
findings.observed: Car drivers see and accept all car rides and rentals; bike drivers also see parcel requests.

findings.title: Customers' trip history, addresses and account details appear to the next user on a shared device — sign-out leaves globally keyed query data cached
findings.observed: Both sign-out controls leave globally keyed me, bookings and trip query data cached.

findings.title: Customers wait indefinitely for a driver after 30 minutes — dispatch silently stops offering the still-searching booking
findings.observed: Requests older than 30 minutes disappear from driver lists but remain searching and active.

findings.title: Customers cannot book when address search is unavailable — neither endpoint of the map supports choosing a point or entering coordinates
findings.observed: Search errors show a toast; the map has no pickup or drop selection handler.

findings.title: A fresh deployment has no usable super admin to approve drivers or manage fares — startup seeds only fares and no admin email is configured
findings.observed: ADMIN_EMAIL is unset; startup seeds no user and new signups default to customer.

findings.title: Approved drivers can see unrelated customers' pickup, phone and parcel details across India — the requests route has no proximity or service-area access check
findings.observed: GET /driver/requests exposes matching vehicle bookings from all locations before assignment.

findings.title: Riders can be charged a different fare from the amount they confirmed — booking silently recalculates using the current fare after the estimate
findings.observed: A pricing edit between estimate and confirmation changes the stored fare without reconfirmation.

findings.title: Customers risk paying twice after a successful Razorpay charge — a failed verification leaves the booking pending and each retry creates a new order
findings.observed: A captured payment with a lost verify request remains pending; retry creates a fresh order.

findings.title: Drivers can bypass a passenger's trip-start safety check by guessing the OTP — the start endpoint allows unlimited attempts
findings.observed: POST /driver/bookings/{bid}/start has no attempt limit or lockout for a wrong OTP.

findings.title: Rental customers can be charged more than the advertised hourly rate — the rental formula applies a separate minimum instead of hours × rate
findings.observed: A 1-hour rental at ₹100/hour with minimum ₹299 is quoted and charged ₹299.

findings.title: Super admins see unpaid online trips as collected revenue and earnings — the dashboard sums every completed fare without checking payment status
findings.observed: Gross revenue and platform earnings include completed online trips with payment_status pending.

findings.title: Drivers and riders are stranded when an assigned driver cannot serve a trip — the driver has no cancellation or reassignment action
findings.observed: Only the customer has a cancel action; an assigned driver cannot cancel a trip.

findings.title: Customers can lose address search and be unable to book — Nominatim calls are not globally rate-limited to its one-request-per-second policy
findings.observed: Each uncached search goes directly to Nominatim; typing triggers requests every 450 ms.

findings.title: Customers can end up with two active trips and two dispatched drivers — the active-booking check and insert are not atomic
findings.observed: Two concurrent booking requests can both pass the active-booking check and insert.

findings.title: One driver can accept two riders simultaneously, leaving a rider unserved — active-driver checking and assignment are not atomic
findings.observed: Two simultaneous accepts by one driver can both pass the active-trip check.

findings.title: Suspending or demoting an on-trip driver strands the rider in an uncancellable ongoing booking — role removal blocks trip completion
findings.observed: Suspension or role change blocks driver endpoints immediately, even during an ongoing trip.

findings.title: Drivers and the operator can lose fares on online trips — payment is requested only after completion and unpaid riders can immediately book again
findings.observed: An online trip completes while unpaid and the rider can create another booking.

findings.title: The operator can record an uncaptured Razorpay payment as paid — verification never fetches the payment's captured status and amount
findings.observed: A valid checkout signature alone sets payment_status=paid without checking capture status.

findings.title: The operator can lose all super-admin access — concurrent role changes each pass the last-admin count before either update
findings.observed: Two admins can concurrently demote each other after both observe two admins.

findings.title: Drivers can create and complete their own trips, inflating earnings and admin revenue — booking creation and driver acceptance do not exclude self-assignment
findings.observed: An online driver can create a matching booking and then accept it as the assigned driver.

findings.title: Customers cannot retry an online payment when verification fails — the checkout callback leaves the payment button permanently busy
findings.observed: The verification catch shows an error but never resets busy, disabling Pay online.

findings.title: Customers can select a location from an old search — address responses are applied without checking which query is current
findings.observed: A slower earlier search response can replace the suggestions for the latest query.

findings.title: Riders see unavailable drivers as nearby and may book with no viable pickup — estimates count all online drivers nationwide
findings.observed: The nearby count includes all online drivers of that vehicle, regardless of location or active trip.

findings.title: A revoked user's token can still access account and trip data until it expires — protected requests verify JWT signatures but never check session revocation
findings.observed: A signed-out session's previously issued JWT is accepted until its token expiry.

findings.title: Customers opening a shared cab-booking link cannot get a quote — the cab route parameter is passed as an unsupported service
findings.observed: A signed-in visit to /book/cab submits service=cab and the estimate returns 422.

findings.title: Indian drivers and admins see early-morning trips under the wrong day — daily totals use UTC date boundaries
findings.observed: Today's earnings and daily booking buckets use UTC dates, not Indian local dates.

findings.title: The admin's platform earnings disagree with driver payouts — commission is rounded after summing instead of per trip
findings.observed: Two ₹32 fares produce ₹52 driver earnings but report ₹13 platform earnings.

findings.title: Drivers' frequently refreshed request lists slow as bookings accumulate — the dispatch index omits the creation-time filter and sort
findings.observed: Missing index: bookings (status, vehicle, created_at descending) for driver requests.

findings.title: Admins' filtered bookings view slows as trips accumulate — service and combined status/service filters lack indexes supporting their newest-first sort
findings.observed: Missing indexes: bookings (service, created_at descending) and (status, service, created_at descending).

findings.title: Admins' driver approval lists slow as applications accumulate — status-filtered applications have no index for their date sort
findings.observed: Missing index: drivers (status, applied_at descending) for the driver approval list.

findings.title: Customers' fare estimates slow as the driver fleet grows — each vehicle option counts approved online drivers without a matching vehicle index
findings.observed: Missing index: drivers (status, online, vehicle_type) for the per-vehicle count.

findings.title: Riders' and drivers' repeatedly polled active-trip checks slow as histories accumulate — owner and active-status indexes are missing
findings.observed: Missing indexes: bookings (customer_id, status) and (driver_id, status) for active trips.

findings.title: Submitting trip ratings slows as a driver's history grows — the average lookup has no driver-and-rating index
findings.observed: Missing index: bookings (driver_id, rating) for the driver rating lookup.

findings.title: Riders selecting a launch service see unrelated vehicle options — all three ride tiles share one unfiltered ride catalogue
findings.observed: Cab, Bike and E-Rickshaw tiles all open service=ride and list every ride vehicle.

findings.title: Drivers and riders lose live pickup tracking without knowing it — geolocation and location-update errors are discarded
findings.observed: A denied location permission or failed location POST is silently ignored while the driver is online.

findings.title: Drivers, customers and admins mistake failed data loads for empty or loading screens — list and dashboard queries omit error states
findings.observed: Failed requests show a perpetual Overview spinner, empty histories, or no request list.

findings.title: Newly approved drivers cannot go online and demoted users retain stale navigation until reload — the profile query never polls or refetches on focus
findings.observed: Approved or demoted users retain the cached role while the app remains open.

findings.title: Riders keep seeing a driver's old name after a profile edit — booking assignments copy the stale driver application name
findings.observed: Saving a driver's new name updates users.name but not drivers.name used for future trips.

findings.title: Customers' trip-start codes are disclosed to administrators before pickup — admin booking responses do not remove OTPs
findings.observed: Admin booking-list and detail responses include each customer's OTP, even when searching.

findings.title: The owner does not receive the requested React Native mobile app and Node.js backend — the implementation is a browser React client with a Python API
findings.observed: The delivered client uses React DOM and the API uses FastAPI/Python, not React Native and Node.js.

findings.title: Customers do not see the driver's updated rating after reviewing a trip — the driver card reads the stale booking snapshot
findings.observed: Rating a completed trip updates drivers.rating but not the booking's displayed driver.rating.

findings.title: Drivers can retain an incorrect average rating after customers rate concurrently — average recomputation and profile updates are not atomic
findings.observed: Concurrent reviews can write an older calculated average after a newer average.

findings.title: Drivers cannot see the customer's fare before accepting a request — request cards render only the estimated driver earning
findings.observed: Request cards show only 80% driver earnings, not the customer's fare.

findings.title: Visitors cannot view the public landing page during an auth-provider configuration outage — the provider blocks rendering the entire router
findings.observed: When auth configuration is unreachable, the entire app renders blank then sign-in unavailable.

findings.title: Admins can silently lose each other's pricing changes — the fare editor submits its entire stale snapshot without a version check
findings.observed: A save from a stale pricing form overwrites another admin's previously saved fare fields.

findings.title: Super admins cannot see user counts by role or booking counts for each status — the stats API and dashboard expose only selected aggregate counts
findings.observed: Stats return customer, approved-driver and aggregate active counts, but no per-role or per-status counts.

findings.title: Admins' user-management screen slows as accounts accumulate — the environment-filtered newest-first user query has no matching index
findings.observed: Missing index: users (env, created_at descending) for the admin user list.

findings.title: Riders see demoted drivers as available and admins see them online — changing a driver's role leaves the driver profile approved and online
findings.observed: Changing an online driver's role leaves drivers.status=approved and online=true.

findings.title: Signed-out riders lose a shared trip link when they sign in — the landing and auth redirects discard the original destination
findings.observed: Opening a shared trip link signed out leads to landing and sign-in returns to / instead.

findings.title: Courier customers can book a bike for a package it cannot carry — parcel weight never filters or validates vehicle options
findings.observed: A 500 kg parcel receives a bike quote and can be booked for delivery by bike.
